rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
BE = Δm c²
N = N₀ e^(−λt)
t_½ = ln2 / λ

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Nuclear charge.** The total positive charge of the nucleus is Ze, where Z is the atomic number and e the elementary charge; it is the nucleus's pull on the electron cloud.  ·  **Shielding effect.** Inner-shell electrons repel outer electrons and cancel part of the nuclear pull; this screening is greatest in multi-electron atoms.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Fission (heavy nucleus → two + 2–3 n + ~200 MeV); fusion (light → heavy + energy, powers stars).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Effective nuclear charge.** Zeff = Z − σ, where σ is the shielding constant; outer electrons feel this reduced attraction rather than the full nuclear charge.  ·  **Trends across a period.** Electrons enter the same shell while Z rises, so shielding changes little and Zeff increases — atomic radius falls and ionisation enthalpy rises.  ·  **Trends down a group.** Each new shell adds shielding that nearly cancels the added nuclear charge, so radius grows and ionisation enthalpy falls down the group.
